A1.justification: Both readable 19-page PDFs describe the same SSLA/SSLA-Det work. Pages 2–19 match in extracted text and rendered appearance; the first-page research content also matches. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection results on Gen1 and N-Caltech101, training and inference timing measurements, and component ablations in Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original detection, timing, and ablation results in Tables 1–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are identical, including mixture-of-spaces states, position-aware projections, scatter-compute-gather training, and the SSLA-Det architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gen1 automotive and N-Caltech101 object-detection tasks. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in each experiment is identical, including the dataset-specific baselines in Tables 1–2, the LSTM comparator in Table 3, and the ablation variants in Tables 5–8.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain identical preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, and timing procedures, including 40 training epochs for Gen1 and 200 for N-Caltech101.

E4.justification: The efficiency-attribution, spatial-sparsity, position-aware-projection, and patch-size ablations in Tables 5–8 are unchanged. Figure 4 retains the same detection examples and failure cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Tables 1–2 report SSLA-L mAP of 0.375 on Gen1 and 0.515 on N-Caltech101 in both versions; timing and ablation results also match.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, Equations 1–8, and supporting derivations are identical. No assumptions, proofs, or formal properties are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about sparse parallel-trainable attention, the first end-to-end asynchronous linear-attention detector, and its accuracy-efficiency advantage.

C2.justification: The explanations of detection failures, hardware-dependent latency, and ablation outcomes are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same discussion of event-image fusion and the accuracy gap relative to synchronous methods.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is identical, including PyTorch and Triton usage, GPU and CPU hardware, hyperparameters, recurrent C++ inference, and the code-repository link.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 50 references are unchanged, as are the distinctions drawn against prior and concurrent methods. The added acceptance notice does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds a first-page sentence announcing acceptance at ECCV 2026 and updates the arXiv version/date markings. The paper's prose, terminology, and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds an acceptance banner in the first-page upper margin and updates the marginal arXiv stamp. All figures, tables, captions, and the layout of pages 2–19 are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 changes only publication-status information and first-page markings. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation are identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
